control: Root user is protected (MFA on, no access keys)
finding: not evaluated (the scanner returned no result - see Method)
fix_console: Sign in as root > Security credentials > assign an MFA device (passkey or hardware key); delete any root access keys. In AWS Organizations, turn on centralized root access management for member accounts.

control: Every console user has MFA
finding: 2 items checked, all passing

control: Access keys are rotated and unused keys removed
finding: 8 items checked, all passing
fix_cli:
aws iam update-access-key --user-name <user> --access-key-id <key> --status Inactive   # then delete once nothing breaks
aws iam delete-access-key --user-name <user> --access-key-id <key>

control: People get permissions through groups, roles or SSO - not attached to users
finding: User acme-demo-1107-ci-deploy has the inline policy deny-everything attached.
fix_cli: aws iam detach-user-policy --user-name <user> --policy-arn <arn>   # after adding the user to a group with the same rights
fix_console: Prefer IAM Identity Center: one login per person, permission sets per job, no long-lived keys.

control: People get permissions through groups, roles or SSO - not attached to users
finding: User acme-demo-1107-legacy-admin has the policy AdministratorAccess attached.

fix_console: Prefer IAM Identity Center: one login per person, permission sets per job, no long-lived keys.

control: Full administrator rights are limited to a break-glass role
finding: AWS policy AdministratorAccess is attached and allows '*:*' administrative privileges.
fix_cli: aws iam list-entities-for-policy --policy-arn arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/AdministratorAccess
fix_console: Replace AdministratorAccess with job-based policies (PowerUserAccess, ReadOnlyAccess, or service-scoped). Keep one MFA-protected break-glass role.

control: Password policy requires long, non-reused passwords
finding: IAM password policy does not require minimum length of 14 characters.
fix_cli: aws iam update-account-password-policy --minimum-password-length 14 --password-reuse-prevention 24 --require-symbols --require-numbers --require-uppercase-characters --require-lowercase-characters

control: Password policy requires long, non-reused passwords
finding: IAM password policy reuse prevention is less than 24 or not set.
fix_cli: aws iam update-account-password-policy --minimum-password-length 14 --password-reuse-prevention 24 --require-symbols --require-numbers --require-uppercase-characters --require-lowercase-characters

aws cloudtrail create-trail --name org-trail --s3-bucket-name <bucket> --is-multi-region-trail --enable-log-file-validation
aws cloudtrail start-logging --name org-trail

control: S3 Block Public Access is on for the whole account
finding: Block Public Access is not configured for the account 453348321107.
fix_cli: aws s3control put-public-access-block --account-id <account> --public-access-block-configuration BlockPublicAcls=true,IgnorePublicAcls=true,BlockPublicPolicy=true,RestrictPublicBuckets=true

control: No bucket is public
finding: S3 Bucket acme-demo-453348321107-uploads has public access due to bucket policy.
fix_cli:
aws s3api put-public-access-block --bucket <bucket> --public-access-block-configuration BlockPublicAcls=true,IgnorePublicAcls=true,BlockPublicPolicy=true,RestrictPublicBuckets=true
# if the bucket serves a website, put CloudFront with origin access control in front instead

control: Data is encrypted by default (S3 and EBS)
finding: EBS Default Encryption is not activated.
fix_cli: aws ec2 enable-ebs-encryption-by-default --region <region>

control: Databases are encrypted, private, backed up and protected from deletion
finding: no matching resources in the scanned regions
fix_cli:
aws rds modify-db-instance --db-instance-identifier <db> --backup-retention-period 7 --deletion-protection --no-publicly-accessible --apply-immediately
# encryption at rest needs a new instance: snapshot -> copy with --kms-key-id -> restore -> switch over

control: No snapshot is public
finding: no matching resources in the scanned regions
fix_cli:
aws ec2 modify-snapshot-attribute --snapshot-id <snap> --attribute createVolumePermission --operation-type remove --group-names all
aws rds modify-db-snapshot-attribute --db-snapshot-identifier <snap> --attribute-name restore --values-to-remove all
